independent_computation.step_1_what_the_effect_is: Per S1/S2, Bloodsong's Spellblade is gated on the holder landing a BASIC ATTACK after an ability ('your next basic attack within 10 seconds'). Expose Weakness is the debuff that empowered attack inflicts on a champion target ('inflict them with Expose Weakness for 4 seconds'). It is an application event tied to an attack by the item holder, not a persistent damage source.
independent_computation.step_2_trigger_gate_at_t_7.5: The disputed row carries attacker = 'main' with skipped_reason = 'attacker_dead'. A dead champion performs no basic attacks, therefore the Spellblade attack that is the sole trigger for Expose Weakness cannot occur, therefore no Expose Weakness application occurs at t = 7.5.
independent_computation.step_3_damage_arithmetic: Number of triggering basic attacks by a dead attacker n = 0. On-hit component = n x (100% base AD) = 0 raw. Amplification component = (8%/5%) x (damage main deals while dead) = amp x 0 = 0 raw. Post-mitigation by S5: post = raw x 100/(100 + R) = 0 x 100/(100 + 119.6) = 0.0 against Aatrox (level-18 armor 119.6, computed from data/champions.json base 38 + growth via base + growth x (L-1) x (0.7025 + 0.0175 x (L-1))). Overkill = max(0, damage - absorbed) = 0.0. So the CORRECT DAMAGE CONTRIBUTION OF THIS LEAF IS 0.0 UNDER BOTH THE OLD AND THE NEW SNAPSHOT - no number in the fight changes either way.
independent_computation.step_4_the_actual_question_is_membership: Since both readings agree on 0.0 damage, the only question is whether a zero-damage, never-fired proc belongs in the combat event ledger at all. Two source-backed rules decide it: (a) S3 defines the main participant's scored contribution as 'total damage dealt ... before its own death' - post-death rows for main are outside the model's own definition of the participant's ledger; (b) S4 states the corpus pins outputs 'a player can verify in-game (custom game / Practice Tool combat log)'. A proc that never fired because its owner was dead produces no combat-log line, so there is no observable to pin. An authored row therefore asserts a game event that does not exist.
independent_computation.step_5_weighing_the_contrary_precedent: S6 shows the engine does keep visible-but-inert rows (execute display row; post-window revive candidate). That precedent covers DISCLOSURE OF A REAL BOUNDARY the model deliberately declines to price (an execute threshold that genuinely exists; a revive that genuinely triggers outside the window). The disputed row is a different class: it is not a priced-but-withheld mechanic, it is an action that is physically impossible for the participant in that state, and the participant's death is already recorded elsewhere in the ledger. The disclosure precedent does not extend to authoring impossible actions.
independent_computation.conclusion: Correct value at this leaf = absent. Removing the zero-damage 'attacker_dead' Expose Weakness row changes no damage number (0.0 either way) and brings the ledger into line with both the model's own scoring definition (S3) and the corpus's game-verifiability contract (S4).

residual_uncertainty: The scenario definition for 'cleaver_bloodsong_roster' (participants, levels, builds, fight window) is not present in data/ or docs/math-foundations.md, so the fight timeline itself - in particular the independent confirmation that 'main' is dead at t = 7.5 - could not be recomputed from the permitted evidence tree. The arbitration takes the old snapshot's own skipped_reason = 'attacker_dead' as the state assertion under test and asks only whether the row belongs; if instead 'main' were alive at t = 7.5 and a genuine non-zero Expose Weakness proc were owed, BOTH values would be wrong.

One genuine risk class worth a targeted check by the change owner (outside this oracle's evidence tree): Expose Weakness per S1 makes the TARGET 'take increased damage from all sources' for 4 seconds, so a debuff applied by 'main' BEFORE its death must keep amplifying ROSTER ALLIES' damage for the remainder of those 4 seconds. Dropping post-death expose_weakness rows is correct only for the APPLICATION event; it must not also drop or truncate an already-applied debuff's remaining window for allies. The disputed leaf itself carries damage 0.0, so it is not evidence either way on that point.
